{{Short description|Russian mineralogist and crystallographer}}
{{primary sources|date=July 2022}}

'''Boris Borisovich Zvyagin''' (April 14, 1921 – September 18, 2002) was a Russian mineralogist and crystallographer.<ref name=Drits2003>{{Cite journal |authorlink=Victor Drits|last=Drits |first=V. A. |date=2003-02-01 |title=Boris Zvyagin (1921–2002) |url=http://scripts.iucr.org/cgi-bin/paper?es0323 |journal=Journal of Applied Crystallography |language=en |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=177 |doi=10.1107/S0021889803001468 |issn=0021-8898|doi-access=free }}</ref> He is a pioneer in the structural study of layer [[mineral]]s by [[electron diffraction]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Zvyagin |first=Boris Borisovich |date=1967 |title=Electron-Diffraction Analysis of Clay Mineral Structures |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-8612-8 |language=en-gb |doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-8612-8|isbn=978-1-4615-8614-2 }}</ref> and is also known for his work on modular structures, including polymorphism, [[Polymorphism (materials science)|polytypism]], and order-disorder structures in crystals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zvyagin |first=B.B. |date=1988 |title=Polytypism of crystal structures |journal=Computers & Mathematics with Applications |language=en |volume=16 |issue=5–8 |pages=569–591 |doi=10.1016/0898-1221(88)90247-7|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2001-09-01 |title=Boris Borisovich Zvyagin (On the occasion of his 80th birthday) |url=https://doi.org/10.1134/1.1405884 |journal=Crystallography Reports |language=en |volume=46 |issue=5 |pages=883–884 |doi=10.1134/1.1405884 |bibcode=2001CryRp..46..883. |s2cid=189795125 |issn=1562-689X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Zvyagin attended [[Moscow State University]] without entrance exams, graduating with a degree in physics in 1944. He worked at the [[All-Union Geological Institute]] since 1949 and was awarded doctor of science in 1963 at the [[Moscow Soil Institute]]. He then moved to the Institute of Ore Mineralogy of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], heading the laboratory there. Zvyagin became a professor of crystallography and mineralogy in 1977 at the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Drits |first=Victor A. |date=2000 |title=Introduction of Boris Zvyagin |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1346/CCMN.2000.0480614 |journal=Clays and Clay Minerals |volume=48 |issue=6 |pages=716–717 |doi=10.1346/CCMN.2000.0480614 |bibcode=2000CCM....48..716D |s2cid=96278205 |issn=0009-8604|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=Drits2003></ref>

Zvyagin was awarded the [[Bailey Distinguished Member Award]] by [[The Clay Minerals Society]] in 2000.
